sentences.text: [matter-of-fact] Thousands of flights in America just got cancelled because the air traffic system went down.
Seventy years ago, that system was a man pushing little plastic boats across a table.
Pilots radioed in where they were, and in a room far away, a man slid a marker called a shrimp boat across a giant map.
So what happened when you flew somewhere that wasn't on the map?
Nothing, because out there pilots just looked out the window and hoped.
[lowering their voice] In nineteen fifty-six, two airliners hit each other over the Grand Canyon, and a hundred and twenty-eight people died.
That crash is the reason the FAA exists.
[matter-of-fact] And plenty of towers still write your flight on a paper strip, so honestly, I'd trust the shrimp boats over that computer.
